meta.note: The single source of truth for Wayfindr's visual language. Nothing may hardcode these values: the dashboard and the widget both receive them from the generator, and scripts/test-design-tokens.sh fails the build if either generated block drifts from this file.

surface.role: Cards, rows, panels — anything that sits on the ground.

surface-2.role: Recessed fills: table headers, inline code, disabled controls.

ink.role: Primary text, and the fill of primary buttons.

rule.role: Hairline separators between rows and sections.

rule-firm.role: Structural borders: table head underline, panel edges.

brand.role: The Wayfindr mark and links. NOT a general UI accent — see ADR 0014.

signal-rest.role: Nothing is wrong and nothing is needed. Replaces the amber that used to mark calm.

signal-hold.role: Degraded or awaiting an operator. A real warning, never a resting state.

signal-stop.role: Someone is waiting, or an action failed.

site.$note: Assignable site identities. Operators pick one per site; it becomes that site's rail in the queues, its transcript chip, its page accent, and its widget accent. Order is the default assignment order for existing installs. Each hue is tuned per theme to land near 4:1 against its own ground -- a wayfinding system only works if every site is equally legible, and the untuned hues ranged 2.19:1 to 5.73:1 on the dark surface. Note ochre darkens rather than lightens: it was shouting over the others.

font.font-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
font.font-cond: "IBM Plex Sans Condensed", "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
font.font-mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

text.$note: Named by the job the type does, not by size — so a screen asks for a role and the scale stays consistent across surfaces.

space.$note: A 4px base. Queue density depends on the low end of this scale being genuinely small.
